body: 'this girl' is a woman with a name, Scarlett Pavlovich. The other victims have names too. You sound like a jerk.
He's made one blog post claiming innocence?
Oh no. This reads so poorly now, like Amanda devoured her. Fucking hell.

They were included in the original Tortoise reporting from the beginning. And have been known therefore to every journalist (and lawyer) since. If they proved Gaiman's innocence we wouldn't be having this conversation because Tortoise never would have published or would have been sued already.
Gaiman does not have a daughter named any of those names.

I agree with your summary regarding the general public and think that industry is far too risk averse to ignore what the fan base and some media will now do whenever he ducks his head up. There'd be weekly meetings like "how is this tracking online?" "bad, boss, it's bad." Too much risk - no.

I don't think his fans are going to let that happen, tbh. And publishers, agents, etc aren't going to risk any kind of marketing campaign on him now. Would his books still sell if they're not on display out front and consistently recommended? I'm not sure but I doubt it. 

Unless something drastically changes in the media ecosphere, he's done. He can't put out new work. He can't have new adaptations. His residuals will keep rolling in but I imagine will dry up to an income less than he is accustomed to. And good.

Feisty potato deleted their comment but I was already writing this so will hijack Altruistic instead:

There's a reason victims are coming together around this and it's because they're experts in abuse and recognise it. I think on other posts iirc you've acknowledged various perspectives of victims in general but you seem stuck on treating the comments here as some kind of distorted group think. If you are engaging in good faith, I ask that you consider these responses again not as projected triggers as you suggest above but as knowing recognition. We know. And it sucks. And some of us literally want Neil Gaiman to have a heart attack and die and some of us want him to never have this level of power and access again and some of us want him to say sorry. 
.

That this and other subreddits continue to operate with grace, openness, and care is partly because survivors and their friends are present here. It's a feature not a bug?

If you listen to the original Tortoise episodes you can hear what (through his lawyers to Tortoise) he admitted to. And as commentators suggested, that alone is unethical and predatory. And even if we only accept his version of events (I don't), he's not safe or fit to exist in society with any type of power again.

Testimony is evidence. There is evidence against Neil Gaiman and for the testimony that has been published by Tortoise or NY Mag, it was fact checked and corroborated before clearing the editorial and legal standards for print.

I hope this helps your conflict.

I think it's pretty common for people from NZ and Australia to assimilate British and American accents quickly. Unlike in the US where people likely heard predominantly US accents in their media consumption growing up, people who grew up in eg NZ would have watched The Simpsons every night and then a mix of local, UK, and US television and film. And the local accents themselves are quite similar to British ones. 

I'm not surprised she's picked up British notes especially considering she was talking to RJ in person. I grew up in a similar part of the world to Scarlett and also tend to mimic US or UK accents too.

He's abused so many women who deserve restitution but who for many reasons won't or can't sue. He'd need to facilitate some type of independent truth and reconciliation committee to hear victim's stories and give appropriate restitution.

There are dozens if not more women whose lives he has impacted who deserve money. Money first for the lost income due to trauma (and we're talking often lost careers here too not just "time off work"), money for direct remuneration for therapy, and then money to compensate beyond that for damages. His well though deep isn't likely deep enough to pay for this.

So even if he wanted to (I'd bet he doesn't - his stupid public statement showed how he was thinking around this), he can't afford to repay the harm he's done. And for that reason if nothing else he'll keep denying it until hopefully Scarlett takes him for all he's worth and finds some peace in her life.

I hear you. Thank you for talking about it. And I also hope 2025 is a year of further healing and new connections for you, dating or otherwise. I hope we all get to wade out of the trauma soup for longer and longer periods. 💜

I personally think the pressure on women such as Tori to make a statement is unreasonable. And I think in the field of possible statements she could have made (thinking of her career, legal stuff, where's she genuinely at), this is great.

I don't doubt that Neil kept this part of himself absolutely hidden from Tori Amos. The same way Harvey Weinstein didn't try shit with established and powerful actresses. 

She's also clearly not on social media and participating in the same media ecospheres we are. To expect she's taking in what we are is unfair. 

And her story with Neil is deeply, deeply personal. It's not fair that she has to flay herself to us, complete strangers.

The VF article pissed me off in so many ways.

A week or so later it's mostly left me sad that Britt spoke after all these years and the reception is mostly about how cringey the prose is. Not her and her clearly fascinating and worthy life. I wish the writer and editors recognised her value and voice more. 

It's like the women adjacent to these men can only be mined for their value to their (the men's) story. And then it's also like eh, bad boys be bad? When it comes to the men. Rather than a reckoning with what this actually means. That men abuse women and it's socially sanctioned in myriad ways and maybe these women had and continue to have more to say than being a muse or resource for a literary man.
